title: A Higher Nominal Growth World Brings Higher Volatility, Says Jim Caron
summary:
Market and policymaker discourse over the next move for the Fed is split: One camp believes the central bank needs to assert its commitment to price stability by hiking in September, particularly to recover some of Chairman Kevin Warsh’s inflation-fighting credibility. 
Another thinks that price gains are on the way down and the Fed is correct to stay its current course.
Jim Caron, CIO of Cross Asset Solutions at Morgan Stanley Investment Management, discusses the shift toward higher nominal growth and how the Fed is set to respond to this week's inflation data. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Europe Gas Prices Surge as Hormuz Deal Prospects Remain Murky

title: Soft US Jobs Cast Doubt on September Fed Hike
summary: Jennifer McKeown, Chief Global Economist at Capital Economics, discussed the implications of the recent US labor market report on Federal Reserve interest rate expectations. The report showed a decline in payrolls alongside a drop in the unemployment rate, presenting a mixed picture. Wage growth at 3.2% was softer than expected, which may reduce the likelihood of an imminent rate hike in September. McKeown emphasized that the upcoming July CPI data and the next payroll report before the September Fed meeting will be critical in shaping policy decisions. She also highlighted concerns about the falling labor force participation rate, questioning whether this reflects structural issues or a mismatch between job quality and worker preferences. Overall, the segment underscored market uncertainty ahead of key inflation data that will influence the Fed's next moves. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Record Sales of Catastrophe Bonds Driven by Wildfires

The segment highlighted how wildfires have significantly contributed to record issuance levels in the catastrophe bond market. Wrosch provided insights into the dynamics driving investor interest and the implications for risk management in the insurance-linked securities sector. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Braskem Creditors Seek Petrobras Capital as Deal Deadline Looms
